cultural.vision_reason: Hand-drawn batik sarong with kepala (triangular pointed panel), papan, and badan sections in classic brown/blue/cream Javanese-style batik coloring — a form of sarong cloth also worn traditionally in Bali, consistent with the claimed Balinese garment attribution.

physical.title: skirt (unsewn); sarong (unsewn)
physical.summary: A (tabby) cotton skirt cloth, a sarung, previously stitched into a tube but now unstitched.  Decorated in hand-drawn batik, with central kepala, space between triangles filled with background filling design, isen, of k.o. ukel pattern, and design of pointed motif in cream, soga and blue detailing.  Papan have flowers and three-leaved motifs alternating in cream, blue and soga on dark blue ground.  Border to top and bottom of cloth and continuing along vertical borders of papan of scrolling stylised flowers with thorny stem.  Badan has large structural design more or less symmetrical about a horizontal axis, suggestive of two supporting columns with two branches above, these in dark blue, decorated with soga patterning and white detailing.  Surrounding this structure is an isen of gringsing against which are semen patterns and lar, the latter uni-directional suggesting which way up the cloth would have been worn.  Has narrow fold at each short side.   [Text written by Dr Fiona Kerlogue, Horniman Museum.]
